primitives.verbatim_quote: To stabilize the training process in a large batch size setting, we develop the adaptive Column-wise Clipping (CowClip).
primitives.assumptions: Embedding gradients vary in frequency; learning rate must remain constant for stability.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When batch size exceeds optimal threshold without adaptive clipping, accuracy degrades due to gradient explosion.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core issue in large-batch CTR training arises from the heterogeneity of feature ID frequencies—popular items generate frequent embeddings, whereas rare ones rarely do. This leads to inconsistent gradient dynamics across embedding dimensions. Standard scaling laws like linear or sqrt fail because they assume uniform behavior. The proposed CowClip addresses this by applying column-wise gradient clipping, effectively normalizing per-feature update magnitudes. This allows stable training even with massive batches. Theoretically, this is akin to a frequency-weighted projection in embedding space, where each column (feature) adapts its norm based on empirical usage. Empirically, this manifests as improved convergence and preserved AUC despite 128x batch size increase. The failure mode occurs when ignoring these disparities—leading to vanishing or exploding gradients. Thus, the key insight is that embedding stability requires per-column adaptation rather than global scaling.
